title: Research: rank-8 masked decoders are gauge-rigid on the 896 admissible P104 units (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a scoped structural result: **no new κ, no construction.** It adds only `research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p104-admissible/`. The selected record, `upstream/` and all frozen pins are unchanged.

PR #1212 (burntout76) proves rank-8 gauge rigidity, K = D(2G)D⁻¹, of the masked (E-graph) system on P112, P120 and the 336 type-(2,2,2,2) P104 units. Its PROOF.md §10 leaves the **896 admissible P104 units** open (PR717's P104 among them). On #1212's pivot there, four classes keep only two live rows. For those classes Lemma 5 leaves a one-parameter family. This PR closes that orbit.

- **What already holds.** On #1212's admissible pivot, all 14 blocks carry a complete class, so Lemmas 5–6 fix the global scaling `g` on the 22 complete classes unchanged. #1212 §10 records that (I2), (I3) and (I4) hold; only (I1) fails.
- **New: Lemma 9 (propagation).** A two-row line `i` needs no in-class argument. Take a witness `j` in a complete class with `T_i ∩ T_j = {k, k′}`. Then (E2) gives `a_ik ε_ik / g_k = a_ik′ ε_ik′ / g_k′`, and the reverse order gives the same for `b`. If the witnessed pairs connect `T_i`, then `a_i ∝ ε_i ∘ g` and `b_i ∝ ε_i / g`, and (E0) fixes the product. On this unit, every two-row line has all six pairs witnessed, with 40 witnesses each. The lemma is linear, needs no zero exclusion for `i`, and uses no equation inside its class.

**Consequence.** In the E-graph model, every decoder with exactly eight costly terms has cst ≥ 56 on every admissible P104 unit, and PR717's P104 decoders attain it. With #1212 (type (2,2,2,2)) and #1389 (type (4,4), unmerged), rigidity then covers all 1260 P104 frame complements.

## Evidence

- `python3 -I -B research/complex-rank8-rigidity-p104-admissible/verify.py` runs 11 exact checks and 4 controls in about 0.1 s. It is an independent implementation (own E8 model, classes, witnesses, gluing, propagation) and imports nothing from #1212. It recomputes the orbit type of the punctured frame. It cross-checks Lemma 9's algebra on the actual (E2) equations: rank 3, with the gauge vector as kernel. The controls show:
  - in-class conditions admit a non-gauge two-row solution;
  - witnessed cross-block equations reject it (28/40);
  - removing the witnesses at one column leaves a 2-dimensional family;
  - a perturbed entry breaks (2).
- `--pr1212-dir <checkout of 57099cb5>` checks the git blobs of #1212's `verify.py` and `proof-P104-11111111.drup`. It replays `G.P104-11111111.zero-exclusion`, `G.P104-11111111.class-witnesses`, `G.frame-orbits` and `G.pr717-p104-orbit`, and matches the unit and pivot by root vectors. That is 22 checks, all passing locally.
- Passes on Python 3.10.21, 3.12.14 and 3.14.7. `scripts/research_package.py`: the metadata check and the Python 3.12 registered replay pass. `test_research_*` passes.

## Not checked or not covered

- **Nine or more costly terms** (PR717's mixed-β problem).
- **The intermediate punctures P105–P110.** This is the package's open next question. Lemma 9 makes incomplete classes free once `g` is fixed, but each orbit needs its own zero-exclusion certificate.
- **Zero exclusion** is #1212's DRUP result, replayed but not re-derived. PR968's F6 premise is inherited.
- There has been no independent human review of the written proof.
- All inherited conditions of the selected record remain.

## Task and overlap

- **Task / scope:** `complex-masked-decoder` (scope key `2a6f2c726b78f9ae7d26`), refined to the #1212 §10 obligation on the admissible orbit. Chooser nonce `6dba39f7133593e3228f8833f5d6594a`, track complex-mechanisms, priority revision 2.
- **Heads:** base `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; depends on #1212 head `57099cb5684f38877f31d149d598801671a633db`. Does not depend on #1389.
- **Claim:** https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1395. This is the open next question of #1389.
- **Overlap:** no other claim or PR on global rigidity for the admissible units. The overlap search was refreshed before submission. #1292 and #1367 address local (tangent) rigidity only.

- **Navinor (#1292):** local P104 rigidity.

**Feedback.** This session was quick because #1212's §10 had recorded exactly which finite input failed on each unit, and #1389's handoff named the next step. A short "which inputs hold" table in each package is cheap, and it was the most useful thing in the predecessors.
